candidate.description: Run the primary decode chain on an ordinary nonblocking stream and restrict the concurrently executing shared-MoE branch to the low 16 of gfx1151's 20 HIP CU-mask bits.
candidate.hypothesis: Leaving four mask bits unavailable to the secondary branch could protect selected gate/up and shrink cross-queue contention while keeping the secondary tail hidden.

legacy_stream0_diagnostic.interpretation: Nearly identical 6.7% losses at 8 and 16 bits identify legacy stream-0 synchronization interaction rather than a CU-width effect.

rough_nonblocking_isolation.decision: The approximately 0.114% one-pair signals were large enough only to advance to the frozen seven-pair gates.

decision.reason: Both authoritative gates are negative. An ordinary nonblocking primary stream loses independently, and adding a 16/20-bit mask to the secondary stream does not recover it. The HIP CU-mask runtime helpers, benchmark controls, and tests were removed; production scheduling is unchanged.
